note: Cross-platform determinism gate. THREE digests, and the split is the point. simulationSha256 covers the trajectory and is the real gate: every wheel target must produce it, and a mismatch WITHOUT a katVersion bump means a platform disagreed. metadataSha256 covers what model_preset() REPORTS, which runs nothing -- it can be re-based when a reporting bug is fixed, without anyone claiming the market changed. sha256 is both concatenated, kept for continuity. v9 was regenerated at the pt-v3 era boundary, when the default preset moved from pt-v1 to pt-v3 and every trajectory moved with it. On 2026-08-23 the metadata half alone re-based: model_preset()'s default argument had been frozen at the literal "pt-v1" while engines ran pt-v3, so the library reported the wrong preset name and one wrong coefficient (momentum_theta) for every run. katVersion did NOT bump, because simulation_buffer() never calls model_preset() and the simulation digest is unchanged -- which is exactly the distinction the single combined hash could not express.
